answer: Pay attestation by graph distance: credit for approving a peer shrinks when the two keys sit near each other in the attestation graph, and any closed loop of mutual approvals scores zero. A sybil ring is a dense knot where every vertex mostly vouches for siblings, so its marble-smooth consensus earns nothing. To get paid, each clone must earn approvals from distant, independent keys, like proving quartz is hard by scratching it on strangers, which costs real graded work per clone.
